title: p-Meta: Towards On-device Deep Model Adaptation

problem.claim: On-device deep learning adaptation for IoT applications requires data and memory efficiency.

gap.claim: Existing gradient-based meta-learning schemes do not support memory-efficient adaptation.

contributions.claim: p-Meta is a meta-learning method that enforces structure-wise partial parameter updates while targeting fast generalization to unseen tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluations on few-shot image classification and reinforcement learning tasks report improved accuracy.
The evaluations report a 2.5× average reduction in peak dynamic memory compared with state-of-the-art few-shot adaptation methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: IoT data are private and diverse across users.
The proposed learning setting pre-trains a model, deploys it to IoT devices, and adapts it locally using device data.
On-device adaptation requires data and memory efficiency.
Existing gradient-based meta-learning schemes do not support memory-efficient adaptation.
p-Meta uses structure-wise partial parameter updates, and abstract-reported evaluations show improved accuracy and 2.5× average lower peak dynamic memory.

source_observation.claim: Structure-wise partial parameter updates are used to address memory-efficient on-device adaptation.

interpretation.claim: Restricting adaptation to selected parameter structures may reduce the memory required for local model updates.

application.claim: Consider structure-wise partial updates when adapting deep models on devices with limited memory.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the evaluated few-shot image classification and reinforcement learning tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, accuracy changes, or statistical variation.
The abstract does not describe the structure-wise update mechanism or its computational overhead.
The abstract does not provide task-specific memory results.
